All seven baselines produce identical rankings ($\tau = 0.786$, $\rho = 0.905$; raw ability scores differ by $< 0.03$ logits, Table~\ref{tab:raw_scores}). G-MFRM achieves nominally higher rank agreement ($\tau = 0.857$, $\rho = 0.952$), but bootstrap $\Delta\tau$ 95\% CI $[-0.071, 0.071]$ includes zero at $N = 8$, though $P(\Delta\tau \geq 0) = 0.927$. On synthetic data ($N = 50$), the improvement is significant ($\tau = 0.922$ vs.\ $0.839$, Wilcoxon $p < 0.001$), confirming the effect is real but below detection at this sample size.

\paragraph{Predictive fit.} LOO cross-validation strongly favors G-MFRM ($\Delta\mathrm{ELPD}_{\mathrm{LOO}} = -55.7$, SE $= 9.4$, $|\Delta/\mathrm{SE}| = 5.9$; \citealp{vehtari2017loo}), with stacking weight 1.0 and all Pareto $\hat{k} < 0.7$.

\paragraph{Ranking accuracy.} The $\Delta\tau = +0.071$ improvement is not statistically significant at $N = 8$ (bootstrap 95\% CI crosses zero; post-hoc power ${\sim}$50\%). Power analysis indicates $N \approx 17$ for 80\% power (Appendix~\ref{app:power}), validated at $N = 20$ where the improvement reaches significance ($p < 0.001$; Appendix~\ref{app:synthetic_calibration}).
